info.title: OpenCRVS API
info.description: OpenCRVS is an open-source civil registration and vital statistics (CRVS) system. A deployment serves several APIs under one domain: the events service (`register.{domain}`, mounted at `/api/events`), the country configuration server (`countryconfig.{domain}`), the gateway (`gateway.{domain}`) and the auth service (`auth.{domain}`). The events and country-config sections of this document are OpenCRVS's own published OpenAPI 3.1 documents for release v2.0.0, committed verbatim as `upstream.yaml` and `upstream-countryconfig.yaml`; country-config component schemas carry a `CountryConfig` name prefix because the two documents give 98 same-named schemas different bodies. The gateway and auth operations (`/token`, `/notification`, `/graphql`, `/ping`, `/config`, `/publicConfig`, `/forms`) have no vendor OpenAPI and are modelled from the OpenFn opencrvs adaptor, OpenCRVS's Event Notification Postman collection and the gateway's own hapi-swagger document. Because the adaptor builds relative paths against a shared domain, all four services are modelled as paths on one server; each operation carries `x-opencrvs-service` naming the host that serves it.

servers.description: An OpenCRVS deployment. `service` selects the host: `register` for the events API under /api/events, `countryconfig` for the country configuration server, `gateway` for the v1 FHIR/GraphQL gateway, `auth` for the token endpoint.

post.summary: Exchange client credentials for an access token
post.description: Auth service (`auth.{domain}`). Authenticates a system client with `client_id` and `client_secret` and returns the bearer token every other call carries.

post.summary: Submit a FHIR birth or death notification bundle
post.description: Gateway service (`gateway.{domain}`), OpenCRVS v1.x event-notification API. Accepts a FHIR document Bundle whose `entry` array carries the Composition, Patient, Observation and RelatedPerson resources of an incomplete birth or death notification. Requires the `notification-api` scope. Removed from the v2 gateway.

200.description: FHIR transaction-response bundle, one entry per created resource

post.summary: Run a GraphQL query against the gateway
post.description: Gateway service (`gateway.{domain}`), OpenCRVS v1.x GraphQL API. One endpoint for the whole v1 query/mutation surface; the request and response shapes depend on the document sent. The schema below models the `searchEvents` advanced search, the only query the adaptor ships. Removed from the v2 gateway, where the events REST API under `/api/events` replaces it.

200.description: GraphQL response. `errors` is present instead of `data` when the query fails.

get.description: Served by every OpenCRVS service (`gateway.`, `register.`, `countryconfig.`, `auth.`) at the same path.

Gateway service. Aggregates the country config's application settings, roles and certificates for a signed-in user. The response shape is not published in the gateway's OpenAPI document, so it is described here as an open object.

200.description: Client configuration. Shape not documented upstream.

get.description: Gateway service. The subset of the client configuration served before login (application config, login config, country logo). The response shape is not published in the gateway's OpenAPI document, so it is described here as an open object.

200.description: Public configuration. Shape not documented upstream.

get.summary: Fetch the v1 declaration form definitions
get.description: Gateway service. Returns the country config's v1 birth/death/marriage form definitions. The response shape is not published in the gateway's OpenAPI document, so it is described here as an open object.

200.description: Form definitions. Shape not documented upstream.

searchFields.description:
Defines multiple form fields that should be searched when this field has a value.
      All specified fields will be combined using OR logic.

      Example: { searchFields: ['mother.name', 'father.name', 'informant.name'] }
      Will search all fields and return a record if any of the fields match the search value.

type.description:
Explicitly specify the field type for searchFields.
      This is required when searchFields is defined, to show the correct control in the UI.
        
      Example: FieldType.NAME for name fields, FieldType.TEXT for text fields, FieldType.DATE for date fields, etc.

label.description:
Explicitly specify the label for searchFields.
      This is required when searchFields is defined.

value.description: The value of the option

searchCriteriaLabelPrefix.description:
This property determines whether to add a prefix (such as "Child" or "Applicant") before the field label
    when rendering search parameter labels — for example, in the search results page to indicate which fields were used in the search.

    For example, a field config like { id: "child.name.firstname", label: { defaultMessage: "First Name(s)" } } would render as "First Name(s)" by default.

    A field config like { id: "mother.firstname", label: { defaultMessage: "First Name(s)" } } would also render as "First Name(s)" by default.

    So, if both child.name.firstname and mother.firstname are used in a search, the resulting search criteria labels would be "First Name(s)", "First Name(s)",
    which is ambiguous.

    Now, if we treat the field ID prefix as a label (e.g., "applicant.firstname" → "Applicant"), and the field label is already
    descriptive — like { id: "applicant.firstname", label: { defaultMessage: "Applicant's First Name" } } — then the resulting

conditionals.description:
In advanced search, we sometimes need to override the default field visibility conditionals.

       For example, Informant fields in the declaration form may have conditional logic
       that hides them based on other field values. Since the advanced search form reuses
       the declaration form config, those same conditionals would apply by default.

       However, in advanced search we often want to make all Informant fields searchable,
       regardless of their original visibility logic. To do this, we explicitly set their
       'conditionals' to an empty array ('[]') in the search config. This ensures they
       are always rendered in the advanced search form.

validations.description: Option for overriding the field validations specifically for advanced search form.

allowedLocations.description: Override the allowedLocations for a location field in advanced search. Use this when the declaration form's allowedLocations references a scope (e.g. record.create) that search-only users don't have — specify record.search scope instead.

anyOf.description: Filters based on user jurisdiction relative to their office location in hierarchy.

type.description: Determines the search type of field. How to match value.

searchFields.description:
Defines multiple form fields that should be searched when this field has a value.
      All specified fields will be combined using OR logic.

      Example: { searchFields: ['mother.name', 'father.name', 'informant.name'] }
      Will search all fields and return a record if any of the fields match the search value.

type.description:
Explicitly specify the field type for searchFields.
      This is required when searchFields is defined, to show the correct control in the UI.
        
      Example: FieldType.NAME for name fields, FieldType.TEXT for text fields, FieldType.DATE for date fields, etc.

label.description:
Explicitly specify the label for searchFields.
      This is required when searchFields is defined.

value.description: The value of the option

searchCriteriaLabelPrefix.description:
This property determines whether to add a prefix (such as "Child" or "Applicant") before the field label
    when rendering search parameter labels — for example, in the search results page to indicate which fields were used in the search.

    For example, a field config like { id: "child.name.firstname", label: { defaultMessage: "First Name(s)" } } would render as "First Name(s)" by default.

    A field config like { id: "mother.firstname", label: { defaultMessage: "First Name(s)" } } would also render as "First Name(s)" by default.

    So, if both child.name.firstname and mother.firstname are used in a search, the resulting search criteria labels would be "First Name(s)", "First Name(s)",
    which is ambiguous.

    Now, if we treat the field ID prefix as a label (e.g., "applicant.firstname" → "Applicant"), and the field label is already
    descriptive — like { id: "applicant.firstname", label: { defaultMessage: "Applicant's First Name" } } — then the resulting
    label would be "Applicant Applicant's First Name", which is redundant and awkward.

    By setting searchCriteriaLabelPrefix to a translation config object, we can explicitly define the desired prefix
    in the country-config > event.advancedSearch configuration. For example: field("child.dob", { searchCriteriaLabelPrefix: TranslationConfig }).

searchCriteriaLabelPrefix.description:
This property determines whether to add a prefix (such as "Child" or "Applicant") before the field label
    when rendering search parameter labels — for example, in the search results page to indicate which fields were used in the search.

    For example, a field config like { id: "child.name.firstname", label: { defaultMessage: "First Name(s)" } } would render as "First Name(s)" by default.

    A field config like { id: "mother.firstname", label: { defaultMessage: "First Name(s)" } } would also render as "First Name(s)" by default.

    So, if both child.name.firstname and mother.firstname are used in a search, the resulting search criteria labels would be "First Name(s)", "First Name(s)",
    which is ambiguous.

    Now, if we treat the field ID prefix as a label (e.g., "applicant.firstname" → "Applicant"), and the field label is already
    descriptive — like { id: "applicant.firstname", label: { defaultMessage: "Applicant's First Name" } } — then the resulting
    label would be "Applicant Applicant's First Name", which is redundant and awkward.

    By setting searchCriteriaLabelPrefix to a translation config object, we can explicitly define the desired prefix
    in the country-config > event.advancedSearch configuration. For example: field("child.dob", { searchCriteriaLabelPrefix: TranslationConfig }).

conditionals.description:
In advanced search, we sometimes need to override the default field visibility conditionals.

       For example, Informant fields in the declaration form may have conditional logic
       that hides them based on other field values. Since the advanced search form reuses
       the declaration form config, those same conditionals would apply by default.

       However, in advanced search we often want to make all Informant fields searchable,
       regardless of their original visibility logic. To do this, we explicitly set their
       'conditionals' to an empty array ('[]') in the search config. This ensures they
       are always rendered in the advanced search form.

BundleEntry.description: One entry of a FHIR Bundle: a `fullUrl` and the resource it identifies.

fullUrl.description: urn:uuid reference other entries point at.

resource.description: A FHIR resource — Composition, Patient, Observation, RelatedPerson, Encounter, Location or Task.

NotificationResponse.description: FHIR transaction-response Bundle returned by the gateway notification endpoint.

GraphQLRequest.description: A GraphQL request document. The adaptor sends the `searchEvents` query.

variables.description: Variables for the document. `searchEvents` takes `advancedSearchParameters`, `sort`, `count` and `skip`.

AdvancedSearchParameters.description: Filters accepted by the v1 `searchEvents` advanced search. Every field is optional; at least two must be supplied.

SearchEventsResponse.description: Response to the `searchEvents` query. The adaptor unwraps `data.searchEvents.results`.

EventSearchResult.description: One row of `searchEvents.results` — a BirthEventSearchSet or DeathEventSearchSet.
